statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 9 of 100 in the low band, sixteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME equity index futures halt that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday is now about thirty-five hours old and removes the very price path this score measures; fifteen of the twenty-four published forward slots lie inside that closure. Stress rises one point to 64 at the top of the elevated band as the weekend escalation record widened overnight to include Houthi drone and missile attacks on Saudi territory, and as CME FedWatch now prices a 25 basis point hike at Wednesday's FOMC at 85.6 per cent. Confidence holds at 86 on a full primary-source re-verification of levels, yields, oil, the event calendar and every published item cited here. Tail remains below the block threshold throughout the closed stretch and reaches the watch band only in the five slots around the scheduled 22:00 UTC restart.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic repository mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and this single shared reading applies jointly to NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, no venue quotes the Nasdaq-100 in fifteen of the twenty-four published forward slots: CME equity index futures halted at 21:00 UTC on Friday and are scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, so there is no gap, no failed retracement and no session extreme available to score. Second, the escalation that did occur overnight is severe but is held in Stress rather than Tail, because Tail measures a pathological price path and no path exists to be pathological. Third, the one genuine structural checkpoint inside the horizon is the scheduled restart, and the five watch-band slots from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 03:00 UTC on Monday are published as a narrow evidence-based danger window rather than as a broad shutdown. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain unaffected by this reading.
headline: Thirty-five hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84, while the Houthis claim drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia that injured two people at al-Tawwal, an Iranian merchant vessel struck off Qeshm has killed one and wounded three, UKMTO reports a separate projectile strike inside the Strait of Hormuz, the Saudi East-West pipeline stays shut with 4 to 5 per cent of global supply off its route, and CME FedWatch now prices Wednesday's FOMC hike at 85.6 per cent.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as a closed weekend requires, and every level was re-verified against primary sources this hour rather than carried over. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91 per cent, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the session high, roughly 4.5 per cent under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. The last quote is timestamped 11 September at 17:15 New York time. VIX fell 11.21 per cent to 15.84 from a 17.84 close, inside a 15.59 to 17.71 range, a notably calm volatility print against this macro backdrop. Rates and oil are equally static: the Federal Reserve H.15 release still carries its 10 September observation at 4.00 per cent for the 3-month, 4.56 per cent for the 2-year, 4.95 per cent for the 10-year and 5.37 per cent for the 30-year, while WTI settled at $100.05, down 2.37 per cent, and Brent at $104.61, down 2.81 per cent.

Two things changed in the last hour, and they point in opposite directions. The escalation record widened: Yemen's Houthis claimed responsibility for launching drones and missiles at Saudi Arabia, with their military spokesman naming a military base in Sharurah in the Najran region, while Saudi civil defence reported sirens and a projectile strike at al-Tawwal that injured two people and damaged buildings. That is a second attack vector against the country that operates the principal bypass around Hormuz, and it sits on top of an already verified record: a merchant vessel struck at about 01:30 UTC off Qeshm and Hengam islands killing one person and wounding three, a separate UKMTO report of a vessel hit by an unknown projectile while transiting the strait, and the East-West pipeline still shut after drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province, with 4 to 5 million barrels a day and 4 to 5 per cent of global supply removed from that route. Against it, a de-escalation channel appeared: Egypt's president and Iran's president met in New Delhi, with el-Sissi urging Iran to make all possible efforts to de-escalate. Monday's meeting in Oman with Iraq and coastal Gulf states is still scheduled, though a signed Hormuz agreement is not reported to be expected from it.

The macro checkpoint also firmed. CME FedWatch now puts a 25 basis point increase at Wednesday's FOMC at 85.6 per cent, up from 48.4 per cent a month earlier, after August consumer prices rose 3.4 per cent year over year with core up 0.3 per cent month over month and producer prices rose 0.4 per cent monthly and 5.4 per cent annually. The current target is 3.75 per cent and the meeting carries updated projections. That is a firmer and more hawkish backdrop than the previous assessment carried, and it raises Stress and sharpens the forward checkpoint without adding anything to Tail, because none of it has yet met a tradeable price path.

The reason this severity is held in Stress rather than Tail is exactly that. Tail measures a pathological price path that denies mean reversion; no such path exists to be measured, since there is no live tape, no gap, no failed retracement and no session extreme to hold. The shared Finviz cross-asset context was read at the start of this run, is stamped 06:48 UTC and therefore inside the 90-minute freshness bound, but reports a partial collection with its calendar section unavailable. Its usable sections are consistent with the verified picture and are used only as delayed supporting context: latest-session breadth positive across technology, communication services and consumer cyclicals, seven of eight megacaps higher, five of seven semiconductors higher, and delayed index futures marks last seen higher with the volatility future sharply lower and crude lower. None of that is live price-path evidence and none of it is used to justify the current Tail action, which rests on the absence of a tape. Every hourly news item published here was verified by direct fetch or verified reporting no later than this assessment timestamp; no scheduled future event is presented as news.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 07:00 UTC on 12 September to 06:00 UTC on 13 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window sits entirely inside the CME weekend closure. Tail opened at 5, stepped to 6 at 09:00 UTC and held there for most of the window, reaching 7 at 05:00 UTC and 8 in the final slot, in normal mode throughout and tracking the closure rather than any directional view; every slot mapped to EA_ON and green. Stress described a shallow arc, easing from 57 to a 50 low at 17:00 UTC as Friday's crude pullback and the Oman talks headline were absorbed, then rebuilding through 52, 53, 56 and 57 to 63 by the close of the window as the weekend escalation reports accumulated and attention turned to the restart. Confidence held an 85 to 87 band, its dip to 85 through the first half of the window reflecting distance from the last print rather than any loss of verified data. Nothing in the window revises a past opinion with later information.
outlookSummary: Fifteen of the twenty-four forward slots lie inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday; the reference contract is scheduled to reopen at 22:00 UTC on Sunday, this horizon's sixteenth slot. Conditional Tail opens at 9 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical conditions, and drifts gradually to 19 through the closure as the interval without price discovery lengthens and unpriced weekend exposure accumulates. It is deliberately held at 19 in the final two closed hours, because a market that cannot trade cannot produce the failed retracements the score measures. It then steps to 24 in the restart hour, the top of the watch band, and eases through 23, 22, 21 and 20 as two-way flow is assumed to return, falling back through 19 and 18 to 17 by the close of the horizon. Those five watch-band slots define the danger window from 22:00 UTC on Sunday to 03:00 UTC on Monday. Stress holds near 63 to 64 through the quiet Sunday stretch, then builds to a 69 peak at the restart on the unresolved supply-route picture, the new Houthi attack vector against Saudi territory and thin reopening liquidity, before decaying to 64 across the Asian session. Confidence declines from 86 to a horizon low of 80 as distance from the last verified print grows, then recovers to 86 once a live tape exists again. Mode stays normal through the closure, is treated as event/whipsaw for the first two restart hours, mixed while early flow is assumed to normalise, and normal again by the end of the horizon. Monday's meeting in Oman, Tuesday's Empire State index and Wednesday's retail sales and FOMC decision with projections all sit at or beyond the edge of this horizon and are treated as checkpoints rather than as priced outcomes.
